Production TLS sync, MOVE and Sent APPEND preserve exact discovered wire names and reopened mailbox state without double encoding; malformed LIST names fail before SELECT and preserve prior state. requirements.requirement: Respect LIST hierarchy delimiters and mailbox attributes.

Unknown attributes are retained and ignored for selectability, while NoSelect is case-insensitively authoritative. Actual TLS sync selects the literal wire name and preserves it after Store reopen; malformed discovery and known NoSelect targets cannot reach SELECT, APPEND, MOVE or delete. Declared mailbox literals above 8 KiB are rejected before reading their payload. This tests parsing, identity and safe target use, not hierarchy-path derivation, NAMESPACE, IMAP4rev2/UTF8 mode, arbitrary response-literal support, independent servers, providers or native UI.

requirements.reason: The production submission path uses separate budgets for connect, greeting, TLS, EHLO, STARTTLS, AUTH, MAIL, every RCPT, DATA initiation, successful DATA progress, terminator and final reply; no aggregate transaction ceiling is imposed. Source tests pin the recommended delivery defaults: greeting/MAIL/RCPT 5 minutes, DATA initiation 2 minutes, successful DATA write progress 3 minutes (16 KiB codec input chunks), and final acknowledgement 10 minutes. A separate 3-minute terminator budget preserves delivery uncertainty if its completion is unknown. Real TLS submission tests exercise production policy and fresh per-recipient budgets; transport tests exercise stalled progress and final replies. Runtime configurability remains an explicit tolerated SHOULD deviation: these intervals are internal constants. The distinct auth-only probe uses one 20-second deadline and never reaches MAIL/RCPT/DATA. These source tests do not prove real external DNS stalls, providers or native UI.

requirements.requirement: Reject CR/LF header injection from every frontend compose mailto path.
requirements.applicability: Dakia mail user agent client; selected feature profile
requirements.reason: The shipped frontend mailto entrypoint is Reader email-body link handling; there is no OS mailto protocol registration in this profile. Actual App search to detached Reader, authenticated renderer message, opaque native compose seed and ComposeApp tests independently inject CR and LF into To, Cc and Subject. The shared compose validator disables Send, rejects click and shortcut submission, never calls api.send and never opens the URL externally. These are frontend production-component assertions, not physical WebKit activation evidence or a claim about a future OS URI handler.

requirements.requirement: Require TLS 1.2 or later for protected email access and submission.
requirements.applicability: Dakia mail user agent client; selected feature profile
requirements.reason: Constrained real servers establish exact negotiated TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 through the shared production IMAP factory and the separate shared production Lettre SMTP factory. SMTP implicit TLS and STARTTLS both authenticate and quit over the observed version. Explicit manual IMAP and SMTP tests first prove an actual OpenSSL TLS 1.1 positive control, then reject identical TLS 1.1-only implicit-TLS servers before credentials; SMTP also proves no AUTH/envelope/DATA. Default source execution is six passed and two ignored, with each ignored legacy test separately invoked and passed, never counted as a default pass. Direct legacy-version refusal is implicit TLS only: STARTTLS has positive 1.2/1.3 negotiation using the same production parameters plus separate certificate-refusal evidence, not a direct TLS 1.1 downgrade transcript. Durable reviewed execution evidence: docs/mail-safety-results/tls-version-profile-2026-10-21.json. No general cipher-suite, revocation or client-certificate certification is claimed.

requirements.requirement: Do not indicate confidentiality without TLS 1.2 and verified certificates.
requirements.applicability: Conditional obligation if a live connection confidentiality indicator is provided; no such indicator is shipped.
requirements.reason: The shipped UI has account TLS configuration labels but no live connection confidentiality indicator. The conditional indicator requirement is not applicable to that absent feature. Configuration labels are not evidence of an authenticated secure connection, and a future live indicator needs new acceptance tests.

requirements.requirement: Validate multipart boundary syntax, quoting and maximum length.
requirements.applicability: Dakia received MIME and composed-message client paths
requirements.reason: Received MIME tests preserve quoted boundary punctuation and exact 69- and 70-character boundaries through complete parsing, selective publication and SQLite reopen; 71-character received boundaries are explicitly tolerated, not conforming input. Actual MailService SMTP DATA capture now asserts three generated nested mixed/alternative/related boundaries are nonempty ASCII, unique, quoted, use RFC 2046 grammar, have no trailing space, remain at most 70 characters and have opening delimiters plus exactly one matching close. Missing-close sensitivity failed the exact close assertion. Source declarations do not replace the separately recorded source, native or provider execution lanes.

requirements.requirement: Use US-ASCII as the default text charset.
requirements.applicability: Dakia received MIME and composed-message client paths
requirements.reason: Absent-charset ASCII remains exact through complete parsing and the production selective MIME decoding function. Valid unlabeled UTF-8 is deliberately accepted as a compatibility tolerance with exact complete/selective text parity after 8bit, quoted-printable and base64 transport decoding; invalid bytes reject without replacement on those same paths. This is not strict US-ASCII-only default enforcement. The named boundary is complete parsing plus decode_mime_part_body, not a public TLS hydration, SQLite-reopen or native rendering claim.

excludedRoles: SMTP relay/MTA routing, DNS MX selection, queue retry and delivery status notification generation are not client submission features.
IMAP server-only obligations and server load/conformance certification are excluded.
List sender endpoint operation and creation of signed mailing-list headers are excluded; receiver-side safety checks remain included.
Full IMAP4rev2 support is not advertised. Selected modern requirements are explicitly indexed.
evidencePolicy: tested means a reviewed assertion is declared at the source boundary; an unchanged source execution report is separately required. gap is unproven, not a product defect or a pass. unsupported describes an actual bounded product profile exclusion, never a missing test.
